title: Construction Bids: Why Google Ads Rarely Reach Public Owners

facts.fact: The article's byline date is October 31, 2026.
The page states that the phrase "Construction Bids" gets about 1,000 searches a month.
facts.quote: "Construction Bids" Gets About 1,000 Searches a Month, in Phrases That Read Like Contractors Looking for Work

facts.fact: The page attributes to one unnamed industry study the finding that design-bid-build was 19% of construction spending, and says that share is shrinking.
facts.quote: Design-Bid-Build Was 19% of Construction Spending in One Industry Study, and It's Shrinking

facts.fact: The page says its example market is Cincinnati and that the construction-website Search ads it collected ran between August 1 and October 30, 2026.
facts.quote: ran between August 1 and October 30, 2026, using Google's Ads Transparency C

facts.fact: The page states that in its example market, no builder's ads used the word "bid" at all.
facts.quote: In our example market, no builder's ads used the word at all.

facts.fact: The page states that public owners post their projects on portals and can forbid bidders from making contact.
facts.quote: Public Owners Post Their Projects on Portals and Can Forbid Bidders From Making Contact

facts.fact: The page states that this guide, Google Ads for Construction Companies, has 16 chapters.
